market_est: UK ~2000 specialist height-safety/rope-access firms; growing with flat-roof/solar boom
defensible_gap: Per-eyebolt re-test CERTIFICATE (serial, 6kN/30s pull-test value, pass/fail, 12/6-mth recert) issued to building manager — no off-the-shelf product exists; incumbents use private internal CRMs not for sale
why_sc_insufficient: SC has no preloaded BS7883 pull-test load fields, per-eyebolt asset serialisation, or compliant per-anchor certificate format; deliverable is a numbered cert to a third party, not a flick-checklist
wtp: ~£30-60/yr or one-time; small firms test 20-200 eyebolts/visit and bill the cert — paying for compliant output is trivial vs liability

defensible_gap: Weak: BS EN 62305 has NO formal documentation/certificate standard (confirmed by training providers), so there is no specific schema to embody as a moat

market_est: UK ~2000-5000 P601-qualified inspectors + thousands of employers requiring 14-month TExT
defensible_gap: HSG258 TExT report has a prescribed structured form (face/capture/transport velocities, filter/fan data, hood index, classification, competent-person sign-off) that generic apps do not embody; 14-month cycle is anti-subscription by design
why_sc_insufficient: SC checklist lacks HSG258 velocity-measurement structure and calculations; competitors are unstructured Word templates from training bodies, not a guided generator; deliverable is a COSHH Reg 9 record shown to HSE on request
wtp: ~£40-80/yr or one-time; P601 inspectors bill per report and face unlimited COSHH fines — compliant structured output is worth paying for
